_note: Station names and line topology (order, interchanges) reflect the real operational Delhi-NCR metro network as verified against official/authoritative sources (DMRC's Aug 2026 network map, NMRC's published Aqua Line station list, Wikipedia cross-checked against multiple secondary sources for Rapid Metro Gurugram and the Blue Line's Noida branch). Per-segment distance_km/duration_seconds are NOT sourced from timetables -- they are computed at load time from flat averages in graph_builder.py (AVG_INTERSTATION_KM / AVG_INTERSTATION_SECONDS / WALKWAY_TRANSFER_SECONDS). Corrections made against the previous version of this file: Yellow Line terminus renamed HUDA City Centre -> Millennium City Centre Gurugram (official DMRC rename); Grey Line fixed from the invented 'Kharkhari Nahar' to the real Dwarka/Nangli/Najafgarh/Dhansa Bus Stand sequence; Airport Express extended to its real current terminus Yashobhoomi Dwarka Sector-25; Blue Line's Noida branch had 5 real intermediate stations (Sector 34/52/59/61/62) missing between Noida City Centre and Noida Electronic City, now added -- single-source verified, re-check if precision matters. Some far-flung extensions (deep Faridabad, deep Noida, the Red Line's Ghaziabad stretch past Dilshad Garden, the Green Line's Bahadurgarh stretch past Mundka) remain intentionally trimmed for confidence -- not part of this pass. Future/under-construction infrastructure (Phase IV corridors, Aqua Line's Knowledge Park V / Botanical Garden / Boraki extensions) is deliberately excluded as it is not operational.

named_interchanges.note: NMRC Aqua Line <-> DMRC Blue Line. Not a shared platform -- a pedestrian walkway between two separately-named stations. Sources disagreed on whether the dedicated IKEA-sponsored overhead walkway was complete; treated as operational per a separate report of an existing ~300-450m pedestrian walkway already connecting the two stations. Re-verify before treating as certain.

_station_metadata_note: Coordinates are sourced for all 239 stations. The 32 Aqua/Rapid Metro entries were checked one Wikipedia page at a time by hand (each has platform_type/platform_count too). 205 DMRC entries were fetched by scripts/fetch_station_coordinates.py, which queries Wikipedia's structured coordinates API (not a regex scrape) and only accepts a match if the returned page title contains every word of the station name -- anything that redirected somewhere suspicious or had no confident match was left out rather than guessed. The last 2 (Pitampura, Mayur Vihar Pocket I) needed a dedicated follow-up: neither had a usable Wikipedia infobox coordinate, so both were resolved via Wikidata's structured coordinate claims, each independently cross-verified against a directly-fetched OpenStreetMap node (not a search-summary guess -- see each entry's own 'note' field for the full verification trail, including a case where a candidate OSM node pair turned out to belong to a different station and was correctly excluded). DMRC entries (except the 2 follow-up ones, which include a note) do not have platform_type/platform_count -- coordinates only. Deliberately NOT included anywhere: fares (a real metro fare is a function of the origin-destination pair, not a single per-station number -- modeling it as one value per station would be structurally wrong, not just unsourced) and train frequency/first-last timings (no official timetable was consulted). Four official renames have turned up so far while cross-checking coordinates, all found incidentally rather than from a dedicated search: Noida Sector 50 -> Rainbow and Rohini East -> Rohini (both applied to the line topology); Pitampura -> Madhuban Chowk and Mayur Vihar Pocket I -> Shree Ram Mandir Mayur Vihar (both NOT applied -- topology changes were explicitly out of scope for the pass that found them, so the stations remain under their existing names with the rename documented in each entry's 'note' field).

Counting only the 2 Pink Line platforms actually modeled here.

Magenta.note: Platform 4 explicitly tagged Magenta; platform 3 only says 'train terminates' with no line tag -- inferred as Magenta since Magenta (not Blue) terminates at this station. Not an explicit label, flagged.

Haiderpur Badli Mor.note: Infobox lists 4 platforms total, but platforms 3-4 are tagged for a Magenta Line extension not in this repo's topology (see ROADMAP.md). Counting only the 2 Yellow Line platforms actually modeled here.

Flagged for a dedicated topology fix; not corrected here since topology changes were out of scope for this pass.

Pitampura.note: Infobox (under the current name Madhuban Chowk) lists 4 platforms total, but platforms 3-4 are tagged for a Magenta Line extension not in this repo's topology. Counting only the 2 Red Line platforms actually modeled here.

Mayur Vihar Pocket I.note: Officially renamed Shree Ram Mandir Mayur Vihar in February 2026 (confirmed via India TV News, https://www.indiatvnews.com/delhi/mayur-vihar-phase-1-metro-station-in-east-delhi-renamed-as-shree-ram-mandir-mayur-vihar-2026-02-07-1029305); kept under the existing 'Mayur Vihar Pocket I' key, topology unchanged, per this pass's scope. Wikipedia has no infobox coordinate for this station under either name -- Wikidata's structured claim (P625, precision 1e-7) is the primary source, cross-verified against OpenStreetMap node 6196100479 (28.6058619, 77.2987023, tagged railway=station, distinct ref=RMAR), agreeing within ~7m. Caution during verification: two other OSM node IDs surfaced by a search-engine summary (6196100478, 6539745133) were checked directly and found to actually belong to a DIFFERENT station (Mayur Vihar-I / ref=MVP1, already in this file under 'Mayur Vihar Phase 1') -- excluded rather than used. No disagreement between the two sources actually used.
